relevance_note: Single case report of a patient with a PSTPIP1 variant and PAMI syndrome: "identified a PSTPIP1 mutation, specifically the heterozygous E250K variant, confirming the diagnosis of PAMI syndrome"; the Discussion also gives individual-level facts on several previously published PSTPIP1/PAMI/PAPA-spectrum patients.
method_note: Read the whole paper; built the JSON with a short Python script from values chosen by reading, and checked every span verbatim against the Markdown by script. In scope: the index patient (label 'patient'); his father (described with severe acne in adolescence, not tested; no variant row); and previously published people from the Discussion with at least one individual-level fact: the p.E101G PAB case [11, 12] and his/her asymptomatic carrier father (sex of that patient not stated); the German mother and son [14] (no variant printed for them; the paper places them among the three colitis cases in PAPA syndrome but does not name their diagnosis or variant explicitly, so disease label and variant rows were left out); the p.T255M case [15]; the p.G403R PAC case [16]; the Japanese case [17] and two Russian patients [18] (PAMI cases; no variant printed, so no variant rows). The son of the [14] mother is labelled by rule 2 ('son of ref [14] patient'). Gene symbol for literature variants (p.E101G, p.T255M, p.G403R) is not printed in those sentences; it is inferred from the paragraph on PAID gene regions and quoted with context spans. Index patient: age 23 at referral recorded as age at last evaluation (follow-up continued 18 months after treatment); age at overall disease onset is not stated (perianal abscess at 15, abscesses at vaccination sites in childhood), so left not reported and onset given per feature; age at diagnosis not stated. Elevated inflammatory markers taken from Table 1 baseline (CRP 92, ESR 97) plus the statement that inflammatory markers normalized; no reference ranges printed. Hypercalprotectinemia not reported: 'Serum calprotectin was not measured'. Short stature (below 3rd percentile) recorded as a feature, but the checklist item 'growth failure or failure to thrive' left not reported because the paper does not call it growth failure. Thrombocytopenia not reported (platelets 148,000 at 18 months, but no statement). 'Septic investigations all came back negative', negative TB PCR/AFB/CMV and normocellular bone marrow were not turned into specific excluded features. 'Otherwise healthy' (father) and 'asymptomatic' (father of [11, 12] case) were not used to exclude specific checklist items. The ileitis of the first Russian patient [18] was not mapped to the checklist 'inflammatory bowel disease or colitis' (ileitis is not colitis; IBD not stated). Functional evidence for E250K is a literature statement about the variant (pyrin binding), not an assay on this patient. No contradictions found in the paper.
